clue.text: One wouldn't appear on it a second time

definitions.text: One wouldn't appear on it a second time

parts.words: One wouldn't appear on it a second time
parts.note: a performer's first public appearance is by nature an occasion that cannot be repeated

explanation.definitionFit: A first appearance on stage or in a team happens only once, so nobody can make it twice.

clue.text: Such a tree would barely survive the winter

definitions.text: Such a tree would barely survive the winter

parts.words: Such a tree would barely survive the winter
parts.note: barely means stripped bare: a tree that loses its leaves stands bare through winter, rather than only just surviving

explanation.definitionFit: A tree that sheds all its leaves each autumn spends the winter with bare branches.

clue.text: Rate beast wrong for dogs' home

indicators.note: letters set wrong are put in the wrong order, so these words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone scores an animal badly for a kennel's adoption listing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrong' rearranges RATE BEAST. Battersea Dogs and Cats Home is a famous London animal rescue centre.
explanation.definitionFit: Battersea is the familiar British shorthand for the London rescue shelter for stray dogs.

clue.text: Record is set at end of race

definitions.meaning: to record sound or video onto magnetic strip
the ribbon stretched across the finishing line that the winner breaks

explanation.surface: An athletics record is confirmed when the race finishes.
explanation.definitionFit: One word covers both recording on a cassette and the finishing ribbon a winning runner breasts.

parts.note: cross means annoyed or angry
a word is an expression in language

explanation.surface: Someone finds a furious remark rather funny.
explanation.definitionFit: This puzzle is a pastime, a form of entertainment solved for fun.

parts.note: closed means shut off from access
a circuit is a motor-racing track

explanation.surface: A racing venue is blocked off so the event can be broadcast.
explanation.definitionFit: A private camera network, as used for security monitoring, is a kind of television system.

indicators.note: doubly says the word that follows is written down twice in a row

parts.note: so means thus, in this way

explanation.surface: Someone is described as twice as apathetic in consequence.
explanation.definitionFit: Middling, neither good nor bad, is what indifferent means in describing quality.

parts.note: O is round in shape
a pine is a coniferous tree

explanation.surface: A forester gives an opinion about the timber surrounding them.
explanation.definitionFit: To give an opinion is to state one's view.

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top, reversing it

parts.note: mined means dug out of the ground

explanation.surface: Fabric has been unearthed by an excavator.
explanation.definitionFit: Denim is a sturdy cotton twill fabric used for jeans.

definitions.meaning: sliced open by a surgeon's knife

explanation.surface: A patient is unhappy after their operation.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both emotionally distressed and literally sliced into, as by a surgeon's scalpel.

clue.text: Preoccupation with sitting next to old boy

indicators.note: next to places the old boy beside the sitting, side by side

parts.note: OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil
a session is a sitting, as of a court or committee

explanation.surface: Someone is fixated on a meeting held beside a former pupil.
explanation.definitionFit: A fixation is a mind wholly preoccupied by one idea.

clue.text: One way to advertise food is on the table

indicators.note: in a down clue, on puts the first piece above the second

parts.note: a sandwich is a common snack food
board means a table, as in board and lodging

explanation.surface: Lunch is laid out on the dining table.
explanation.definitionFit: Two hinged placards worn front and back by a person walking the streets publicise a business.

definitions.meaning: pulled in, as a crowd-pleaser did

explanation.surface: A painter's work proved appealing.
explanation.definitionFit: The past tense covers both sketching a picture and pulling in a crowd.

clue.text: You won't get much change out of this girl

definitions.text: You won't get much change out of this
definitions.meaning: a coin of the smallest value leaves nothing to give back

explanation.surface: A girl is hard to influence or sway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not get much change out of' someone is a British idiom for failing to sway them; here it is read literally about money.
explanation.definitionFit: It is both the lowest-value British coin and a common girl's name.

definitions.meaning: a word used to name something
a span of time, such as a school session

explanation.surface: A label applied to a span of time.
explanation.definitionFit: One word means both a word that names something and a fixed span such as a school semester.

indicators.note: almost means the last letter is dropped from the phrase

parts.note: to harp on is to keep complaining about something

explanation.surface: A grumbler almost goes on about the communist philosopher.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost' drops the final N from HARP ON. Harpo was one of the silent comedy Marx Brothers; the surface tempts us towards Karl.
explanation.definitionFit: Harpo was the mute, harp-playing member of the Marx Brothers comedy team.

indicators.note: in a down clue, upside-down means the word is read from the bottom up, reversed

parts.note: art means pictures and paintings
taken as written

explanation.surface: Paintings displayed wrongly in a bus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hung upside-down' reverses ART to give TRA.
explanation.definitionFit: To coach someone is to train them; as a noun both are railway carriages too.

clue.text: Document the police may need to look over

definitions.text: Document the police may need to look over

parts.words: Document the police may need to look over
parts.note: a court paper authorising officers to examine premises

explanation.definitionFit: Officers need such a legal authorisation from a magistrate before inspecting private property.

clue.text: A British range? No, an Italian

definitions.text: A British range? No, an Italian

parts.words: A British range? No, an Italian
parts.note: A followed by the northern English hill chain looks British, but the whole is a mountain chain in Italy

explanation.walkthrough: The Pennines are the hills forming the 'backbone of England'; put A in front and you get the Italian chain.
explanation.definitionFit: The Apennines are the mountain chain running down the length of Italy.

parts.note: read can as a noun, a tin, and the tool is what gets into it

explanation.definitionFit: A kitchen gadget for cutting open food tins is how one gets inside a can.

clue.text: Abrupt habit of sailing close to the wind

parts.note: sharp means abrupt or curt
a practice is a habit or custom

explanation.surface: A curt manner shown by a yachtsman taking risks.
explanation.definitionFit: Dishonest dealing that is barely legal is idiomatically called sailing close to the wind.

clue.text: Naomi turned back without one complaint

indicators.note: without says a letter is left out
turned back says the name is read in reverse

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Naomi turned around and left with no grumble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned back' reverses NAOMI to IMOAN; 'without' then removes I (one).
explanation.definitionFit: A moan is a grumble or complaint.

clue.text: Many a harsh cry from this bird

parts.note: M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, so many
caw is the harsh call of a crow

explanation.surface: A loud squawking comes from a noisy bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A macaw is a large, brightly coloured parrot.

parts.note: a gent is a gentleman, a decent chap

explanation.surface: A delegate turns out to be a nice man.
explanation.definitionFit: An agent is someone who acts on another's behalf.

indicators.note: entering puts the hesitation inside the reworked word
new says the letters of job are put in a new order

parts.note: um is the sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: A huge pause before starting a fresh job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges JOB as J..BO and 'entering' puts UM inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Jumbo means very large, as in a jumbo jet.

definitions.meaning: a children's game where players call out on matching cards

explanation.surface: Someone stops a game of cards.
explanation.definitionFit: One word means both to break with a crack and a simple game of matching cards.

clue.text: Fight with a piece of wood

definitions.meaning: a pole or boom, as on a ship

explanation.surface: Someone brawls using a plank.
explanation.definitionFit: It means both to box in practice and a stout pole such as a mast.

definitions.meaning: a cricket fielder standing beside the wicketkeeper

explanation.surface: A cricketer in the field has blundered.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, slip is a fielding position close behind the batsman, and the player there takes the name; 's stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: It names both a cricket fielding position and a minor error.

clue.text: Queen of Egypt saw palace rot, sadly

indicators.note: sadly says things have gone wrong, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A Pharaoh's widow watched her royal residence fall to ruin.
explanation.definitionFit: She was the last ruling queen of the Ptolemaic dynasty in Egypt.

indicators.note: changed says the name's letters are put in a different order

explanation.surface: The Soviet leader put on fresh pants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changed' rearranges LENIN. 'Linen' is an old term for underclothes, once made of the fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: Linen once meant body clothing such as shirts and undergarments, made from flax cloth.

parts.note: water is something to drink
shed means dropped, as leaves or skin

explanation.surface: Someone lets a beverage fall at a crucial moment.
explanation.definitionFit: A turning point is figuratively called a watershed, like the ridge dividing river systems.

definitions.meaning: someone who sits for an artist or photographer

explanation.surface: A fashion model is a mystery.
explanation.definitionFit: It means both someone striking attitudes for a camera and a baffling problem.
